name: Citigroup

summary.text: Citigroup Inc. is a New York-based global bank. On this site it appears through its Enron-era prepay transactions, for which it paid $120 million in a July 2003 SEC settlement, without admitting or denying wrongdoing, over structured deals that helped Enron and Dynegy characterize loan proceeds as operating cash flow. In November 2008 the U.S. Treasury, Federal Reserve and FDIC agreed to guarantee losses on a roughly $306 billion pool of Citigroup assets, and the government invested a total of $45 billion in Citigroup under TARP. In August 2022 Citi announced the wind-down of its consumer and local commercial banking businesses in Russia.

facts.claim: On July 28, 2003 Citigroup consented to an SEC administrative cease-and-desist order and agreed to pay $120 million ($101.25 million allocable to Enron and $18.75 million to Dynegy) to settle charges that it helped Enron mislead investors by characterizing what were essentially loan proceeds as cash from operating activities. Citigroup did not admit or deny wrongdoing. The same day it agreed to pay $25.5 million under a settlement with the Manhattan District Attorney, and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and the OCC reached agreements on its Enron transactions.
facts.quote: helping Enron mislead its investors by characterizing what were essentially loan proceeds as cash from operating activities

facts.claim: On November 23, 2008 the Treasury, Federal Reserve and FDIC announced that Treasury and the FDIC would provide protection against unusually large losses on a pool of approximately $306 billion of Citigroup loans and securities backed by residential and commercial real estate and other assets, which would remain on Citigroup's balance sheet. Citigroup would absorb the first $29 billion of losses pre-tax in addition to existing reserves, with the government assuming 90% of losses above that level, and Citigroup would issue preferred shares to Treasury and the FDIC as a fee.
facts.quote: protection against the possibility of unusually large losses on an asset pool of approximately $306 billion of loans and securities

facts.claim: The U.S. government invested a total of $45 billion in Citigroup under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act: $25 billion under the Capital Purchase Program and $20 billion in exceptional assistance under the Targeted Investment Program. Treasury later described the loss-sharing arrangement as covering approximately $301 billion of assets under the Asset Guarantee Program and reported that Citigroup repaid the $20 billion in exceptional assistance.
facts.quote: The U.S. government invested a total of $45 billion in Citigroup under the EESA.

facts.claim: On August 25, 2022 Citi announced it would wind down its consumer banking and local commercial banking operations in Russia, expanding an exit begun in April 2021 as part of a plan to leave consumer banking in 14 markets and widened in March 2022. Citi expected about $170 million in costs over roughly 18 months, with about 2,300 employees and 15 branches affected; its remaining Russia exposure was $8.4 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2022, down from $9.8 billion at year-end 2021.
facts.quote: Citi will wind down its consumer banking and local commercial banking operations in the country.

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): 'JPMorgan Chase and Citigroup executed Mahonia/Yosemite prepay transactions — loans disguised as commodity sales' is supported in substance by the SEC's 2003 settlement description; the SEC release uses 'prepay' and 'loan proceeds' rather than the Mahonia/Yosemite vehicle names, which were not confirmed from the pages opened.
The exact Treasury press release number tg573 and its date were not confirmed from the snippet; the owner should check the URL.
Citigroup's 2004 acquisition of KorAm Bank is recorded in the carlyle-group file and was not duplicated here.
Any role of Citigroup in Russian privatization or 1990s Russia (if that is what the brief's 'Russia role' refers to) was not researched; only the 2022 wind-down was documented.
